process_area.title: Site Cleanup Service Design, Estimation & Crew Scheduling

value_stream.name: Customer Construction Debris, Demolition Waste & Site Cleanup Operations

fields.Frequency: Annual review; new product/SKU as needed
fields.Trigger: Service launch; annual pricing review; new install/build channel introduction
fields.Volume: ~8–15 service products (post-install cleanup, post-demolition cleanup, bulk-debris haul, skip rental, final handover clean)

workflows.name: Site Cleanup Service Product Design, Pricing & Catalog

Automation Opportunity: - Attach-rule automation at order entry; distance/zone-based hauling-cost calculator; periodic cost-re-forecast feed from disposal-vendor invoices.
Controls: - CTL-803 (ensure controlled execution — Site Cleanup Service Design, Estimation & Crew Scheduling (PA-191.1).)
- operational: service/pricing approval; Consumer Act disclosure in service terms; hazardous/regulated materials explicitly excluded in service terms.
Cross-references: - links to VS-12 (installation), VS-66 (design-build), VS-143 (appliance install), VS-70 (solar), VS-184 (disaster repair), VS-29 (service items), VS-08/VS-10/VS-11 (attach)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mispriced-haul risk**: under-pricing hauling/disposal (long haul distance, landfill tip fees, demurrage) erodes margin or loses money on every job; mitigated by cost-plus pricing with distance/zone and periodic cost re-forecast.

- **Scope-creep risk**: customers expect "cleanup" to include hazardous/regulated removal (asbestos/lead/paint) the service excludes; mitigated by explicit service terms and the W5443 pre-job assessment.
System Touchpoints: - Service-item master (VS-29); pricing (VS-01.2/VS-101); POS/order attach (VS-08/VS-10/VS-11); catalog/PIM (VS-137); compliance records (VS-22/VS-100).
Time Estimate: - ~2–3 weeks/annual pricing review; ~3–5 days/new product launch.

steps.activity: Define the site-cleanup service catalog tied to BuildRight's install/build channels (post-appliance-install, post-tile/flooring, post-projects/VS-66, post-solar/VS-70, post-disaster-repair/VS-184, final handover clean).
Price each service on container-cube + crew-hours + hauling/disposal cost + margin, accounting for scrap-metal recovery and diversion-rebate offsets.
Configure service items/SKUs and attach-to logic at POS/order entry so cleanup is offered with every qualifying install/build sale (links VS-08/VS-10/VS-11).
Legal review of service terms (LGU/DENR liability boundary, hazardous exclusion, indemnity) and Consumer Act (RA 7394) disclosure.
Publish to the website/app/Pro-Desk catalog and train sales associates (VS-124) on attach.

fields.Frequency: Per cleanup engagement — ~thousands/yr across install base
fields.Participants: Sales Associate (VS-124), Installation Supervisor (VS-12), customer, Estimation (VS-09.2)
fields.Trigger: Customer inquiry at POS/Pro-Desk/online; install/build sale; site survey

workflows.name: Customer Debris Volume & Container Size Estimation

Automation Opportunity: - Channel-standard volume tables auto-suggested from the originating sale's SKUs (e.g., a tile-job's expected rubble); photo-assisted volume estimation; distance/zone auto-rate.
Controls: - CTL-803 (ensure controlled execution — Site Cleanup Service Design, Estimation & Crew Scheduling (PA-191.1).)
- operational: estimate accuracy/evidence; quote approval threshold; site survey required above a volume/value threshold.
Cross-references: - links to VS-09.2 (takeoff/estimation), VS-12 (install scope), VS-11/VS-10 (quote/booking), VS-143 (appliance-install attach)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-estimated-volume risk**: under-sized container/truck → overflow, extra trips, margin loss, and customer dissatisfaction; mitigated by conservative sizing tables and site-survey-for-large-jobs policy.

- **Access-misjudgment risk**: a container that can't physically fit the site (narrow lane, no parking, condo rules) strands the job; mitigated by mandatory access capture in the estimate and skip-placement permit (W5445).
System Touchpoints: - Service-item/quote module (VS-11/VS-10); takeoff tools (VS-09.2); volume/weight conversion library; photo/attachment store; distance/zone rate engine (W5441).
Time Estimate: - ~10–20 min/routine post-install estimate; ~1–2 hours + site visit for large/project jobs.

steps.activity: Gather job parameters: scope (e.g., post-kitchen-reno, post-tile job, full demolition), material mix (wood/drywall/masonry/metal/packaging), site access (stairs, elevator, parking, hauling distance).
Estimate debris volume (cubic meters) and weight using standard conversion factors per material class; select container/skip size (2/5/10/20 cu.m.) or truck trips.
For larger/project jobs, schedule a site survey (VS-09.2 takeoff) to validate; for routine post-install, use channel-standard tables.
Quote price (W5441 catalog + distance/zone) and present options (one-off haul, scheduled multi-haul, skip rental period).
Document the estimate and assumptions (photos/site sketch for larger jobs) to support W5448 booking and any post-job dispute.

fields.Participants: HSE (VS-24), customer, Estimator (VS-09.2), VS-187 hazmat, VS-73 asbestos (W2613)
fields.Trigger: Booking confirmed (W5448); any demolition/suspect-older-building job; post-disaster (VS-184)
fields.Volume: Per cleanup job; ~100% of demolition/large jobs screened

workflows.name: Job Site Cleanup Pre-Job Hazard & Regulated-Material Assessment

Automation Opportunity: - Suspect-material decision tree in the work-order; auto-routing to abatement/TSD vendors; JHA template auto-populated from job type.
Controls: - CTL-803 (ensure controlled execution — Site Cleanup Service Design, Estimation & Crew Scheduling (PA-191.1).)
- operational: DENR RA 6969 regulated-material routing; abatement-specialist segregation; no demolition job proceeds without a documented hazard assessment.
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE/JHA), VS-73 W2613 (asbestos abatement), VS-187 (hazmat TSD), VS-184 (post-disaster hazards), VS-114 (DG transport if any)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Asbestos-mishandling risk**: drywall/ceiling/insulation debris containing asbestos, swept into a standard C&D load, creates a serious health and DENR (RA 6969) liability; mitigated by mandatory suspect-screening and abatement routing.
- **Crew-injury risk**: an unrehearsed demolition/structural hazard injures cleanup crew; mitigated by JHA + PPE + HSE sign-off before crew dispatch.
System Touchpoints: - JHA/hazard-assessment module (VS-24); asbestos/lead abatement records (VS-73 W2613); hazmat TSD records (VS-187); work-order (W5448); photo/evidence store.
Time Estimate: - ~20–40 min/routine screening; ~2–4 hours + specialist for demolition/suspect jobs.

steps.activity: Screen the job for regulated/hazardous materials: asbestos/lead suspect (pre-1990s buildings), paint/solvent residues, refrigerants, treated wood, chemical containers, e-waste.
For suspect asbestos/lead, route to the accredited abatement path (VS-73 W2613) — do NOT include in standard C&D hauling; pause the cleanup until resolved.
For household hazardous residues, route to VS-187 take-back or accredited TSD; exclude from the mixed C&D load.
Capture site hazards (live utilities, structural instability, confined space, working at height) and brief the crew with a job-hazard-analysis (JHA) and required PPE.
Document the assessment and customer acknowledgment of scope/exclusions; update the work order (W5448).

fields.Participants: Crew leads, Fleet (VS-06), hauling 3PL (VS-56/VS-110), Store/DC, customer

Automation Opportunity: - Route optimization across jobs; capacity-aware auto-assignment; real-time ETA and exception alerts.
Controls: - CTL-803 (ensure controlled execution — Site Cleanup Service Design, Estimation & Crew Scheduling (PA-191.1).)
- operational: scheduling/dispatch accuracy; change management on exceptions; permit-before-placement sequencing.
Cross-references: - links to VS-06 (fleet), VS-56/VS-110 (3PL hauling), VS-74 (jobsite delivery), VS-12 (install crew coordination)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Subutilization risk**: poorly-routed crews/trucks run empty or sit idle, eroding the service margin; mitigated by clustering and capacity-aware scheduling.
- **Permit-blocked-placement risk**: a container delivered before its LGU placement permit (W5445) is issued is refused or towed; mitigated by permit-before-placement sequencing.
System Touchpoints: - Dispatch/routing system (VS-06/VS-56/VS-74); fleet/3PL capacity (VS-06/VS-56); mobile work-order app; telematics (VS-06 W199); container fleet register (W5445).
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 hours/day dispatch planning per region; ~5–10 min/job dispatch confirmation.

steps.activity: Schedule the crew, container delivery, and haul truck against the booking window and site access constraints (W5442).
Optimize routing across multiple jobs/region (cluster nearby jobs, minimize empty haul miles) — coordinate with fleet/3PL capacity (VS-06/VS-56).
Confirm container/skip placement and LGU permit (W5445), crew certification/PPE (W5443), and customer site readiness.
Dispatch with mobile-app work order, route, JHA, and regulated-material flags; track arrival/time-on-site.
Handle exceptions (access denial, volume overrun, weather, hazardous discovery) via the dispatch escalation path.

fields.Frequency: Per job placement; ongoing fleet sourcing
fields.Trigger: Service setup; per skip-rental job; container-fleet refresh
fields.Volume: ~30–50 owned/leased containers + per-job LGU placement permits

workflows.name: Skip/Dumpster & Container Fleet Sourcing, Placement & LGU Permit

Automation Opportunity: - Permit-status tracking integrated to dispatch (block drop until permit issued); container telematics/dwell auto-billing.
Controls: - CTL-803 (ensure controlled execution — Site Cleanup Service Design, Estimation & Crew Scheduling (PA-191.1).)
- operational: LGU permit compliance; container-fleet register; demurrage accuracy; operational: permit-before-placement for any public-right-of-way occupancy.
Cross-references: - links to VS-76 (LGU permits), VS-166 (license/permit portfolio), VS-34 (procurement), VS-06 (fleet), VS-35 (asset register)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unpermitted-occupancy risk**: an on-street container without LGU/Barangay permit is towed/fined (LGU ordinance); mitigated by permit-before-placement and VS-76 LGU coordination.
- **Container-loss/theft risk**: containers left on customer/street sites are stolen or abandoned; mitigated by GPS/telematics on the fleet and dwell-tracking.
System Touchpoints: - Asset/container-fleet register (VS-35 extended); LGU permit records (VS-76/VS-166); dispatch (W5444); demurrage billing (VS-11/VS-15); fleet (VS-06).
Time Estimate: - ~1–3 days lead for LGU permit (varies by LGU); ~10–20 min/placement planning.

steps.activity: Source/maintain the skip/dumpster/container fleet (own + leased + 3PL) sized to service demand across regions (2/5/10/20 cu.m. sizes).
For each placement, secure the LGU/Barangay permit to occupy public road/right-of-way (where the container sits on-street) per VS-76.
Confirm placement plan with the customer (driveway vs street vs private property, surface protection, accessibility).
Coordinate container drop with the hauler/fleet (VS-06/VS-56) and the crew schedule (W5444).
Track container location/dwell; manage demurrage billing for over-dwell beyond the rental period.

fields.Frequency: Per B2B project; ~hundreds of project engagements/yr
fields.Participants: Services Manager, Estimator (VS-09.2), Pricing, Legal (VS-100), Customer PM
fields.Trigger: B2B project award (VS-11/VS-66); developer/contractor/LGU bulk-debris engagement
fields.Volume: B2B project debris from developers/contractors/government — large multi-haul

workflows.name: B2B Project & Bulk Debris Engagement, SLA & Quotation

Automation Opportunity: - Project-phase debris forecasting from the project plan; SLA dashboard; change-order volume alerts.
Controls: - CTL-803: ensure controlled execution — Site Cleanup Service Design, Estimation & Crew Scheduling (PA-191.1).) — project pricing/contract approval; CTL-21 (estimate accuracy; CTL-34 (LGU/DENR liability terms); operational: phase-gated re-estimation on B2B projects.
Cross-references: - links to VS-11 (B2B project), VS-107 (key account), VS-66 (design-build), VS-77 (material staging), VS-09.2 (takeoff), VS-100 (contracts)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-scoped-project-volume risk**: a project's actual debris volume far exceeds estimate (hidden demolition, change orders), eroding the contract margin; mitigated by phase-gated re-estimation and change-order pricing.

- **Diversion-target-breach risk**: a B2B customer's sustainability KPI requires a diversion rate BuildRight can't meet on a particular site; mitigated by realistic diversion commitments upfront and W5457 diversion planning.
System Touchpoints: - B2B project module (VS-11); quotation/contract (VS-100); progress billing (VS-11); SLA/KPI tracking; VS-77 staging plan.
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 weeks per B2B project engagement/scoping; ongoing through the project term.

steps.activity: Engage with the project owner/contractor to scope debris over the project lifecycle (demolition phase, construction phase, handover) — link to VS-77 material staging and VS-11 project plan.
Estimate total debris volume/stream over project phases and design the hauling schedule (recurring multi-haul vs. on-call).
Quote with B2B project pricing (volume tier, dedicated container, SLA, diversion targets) and contract terms (LGU/DENR liability, indemnity, demurrage).
Define SLAs (response time, hauling cycle, diversion rate, reporting) and KPIs for the project term.
Book as a project work order with milestone billing (VS-11 W165/W1288 progress billing) and integrate into the project site plan.

fields.Trigger: Service launch; capacity expansion to a new region; vendor renewal/exit

Automation Opportunity: - Permit/accreditation expiry monitoring (links VS-166 license-portfolio); manifest receipt and chain-of-custody digital record; capacity/cost vendor scorecard.
Controls: - CTL-803: DENR RA 9003/6969 accredited-disposer verification; CTL-803 (TPRM/vendor risk, links to VS-161); CTL-44 (duplicate-invoice/manifest guard); operational: chain-of-custody manifest required for every C&D load.
Cross-references: - links to VS-110 (freight procurement), VS-56 (3PL), VS-34 (procurement), VS-161 (TPRM), VS-22 (DENR permits), VS-166 (license portfolio)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unaccredited-disposer risk**: a hauler taking C&D to an unpermitted dumpsite creates illegal-dumping liability for BuildRight (RA 9003/RA 6969) even if the hauler acted independently; mitigated by DENR accreditation verification and chain-of-custody manifests.
- **Vendor-concentration risk**: a region with a single hauler/disposer fails if that vendor lapses; mitigated by fallback vendors and capacity monitoring.
System Touchpoints: - Vendor master (VS-03/VS-29); TPRM (VS-161); DENR permit records (VS-22); contract management (VS-100/VS-34); dispatch (W5444).

steps.activity: Qualify hauling subcontractors on LGU hauling permit, DENR transporter registration, vehicle/insurance, and capacity; integrate with VS-110 freight and VS-56 3PL.
Qualify accredited disposers/recyclers/landfills: DENR-EMB-accredited TSD/MDRF/sanitary landfill, recycler reprocessing accreditation; verify permits (VS-22) and TPRM tier (VS-161).
Contract with waste-stream acceptance terms (clean wood, masonry, metals, mixed C&D), manifest/digital-record obligations, chain-of-custody, and audit rights.
Onboard into the dispatch system (W5444) with capacity, region, and acceptance-stream data; define fallback vendors for continuity.
Periodically recertify permits/accreditation and audit a sample of manifests; manage exit/replacement on lapse or performance failure.

workflows.name: Site Cleanup Service Work Order, Pricing & Booking Confirmation

Automation Opportunity: - Estimate-to-work-order conversion; automated confirmation touches; PFRS 15 performance-obligation tagging; no-show-prediction alerts.
Controls: - CTL-803 (ensure controlled execution — Site Cleanup Service Design, Estimation & Crew Scheduling (PA-191.1).)
- operational: work-order/pricing accuracy; Consumer Act disclosure; revenue recognition — PFRS 15; operational: documented cancellation/refund policy.
Cross-references: - links to VS-157 (revenue recognition), VS-15 (billing/AP for vendors), VS-13 (customer), VS-29 (master data), VS-75 (app notification)
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-show/late-cancellation risk**: customer cancels after container/crew are committed, stranding cost; mitigated by cancellation policy with retention/fee and confirmation-touch before dispatch.
- **Revenue-recognition-error risk**: recognizing cleanup revenue at booking rather than completion distorts PFRS 15; mitigated by the service-completion trigger (VS-157).
System Touchpoints: - Work-order/service module; CRM/customer (VS-13/VS-29); notification (app/SMS/VS-75); revenue recognition (VS-157); dispatch handoff (W5444).

steps.activity: Convert the accepted estimate into a service work order: scope, container/truck, crew, schedule, price, terms, exclusions.
Apply Customer Act (RA 7394) disclosures (service description, price, cancellation/refund policy, hazardous exclusion) and capture customer acknowledgment.
Confirm booking with the customer (date/window, access requirements, prep, what to expect) via app/SMS/email.
Set up revenue recognition per PFRS 15 (performance obligation satisfied at service completion; or over a multi-haul contract period) — link VS-157.
Trigger dispatch scheduling (W5444) and record the booking in the work-order system for execution (W5449) and settlement (W5457).
